q: Which body of eminent professionals and officials replaced the Government's Appointments Board for choosing whole-time directors and non-executive chairmen of public sector banks?
explain: The Banks Board Bureau, which began working on 1 April 2016, replaced the Appointments Board and recommends heads of PSBs.

q: The Banks Board Bureau was set up on the basis of the recommendations of which committee?
explain: The Committee to Review Governance of Boards of Banks in India (May 2014), chaired by P J Nayak, recommended the Bureau.

q: Besides the Chairman, how many members does the Banks Board Bureau have?
explain: It has 3 ex-officio members from the Government and 3 expert members (two from the private sector), i.e. six members besides the Chairman.

q: From which date did the Banks Board Bureau start functioning?
explain: The Bureau started working on 1 April 2016. Its constitution and composition had been announced on 28 February 2016.

q: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Banks Board Bureau?
options: Recommending appointments of full-time directors of PSBs
Advising banks on mergers and consolidation
Approving corporate credit proposals of banks
Advising PSBs on handling stressed assets
explain: Loan approvals are a bank's own business. The BBB recommends heads, advises on fund-raising and stressed assets, and guides on mergers and governance.

q: In which year was the Indian Banks' Association (IBA) formed?
explain: IBA was formed on 26 September 1946 in Mumbai as a representative body of bank management. 1934 is the year of the RBI Act.

q: Who served as Chairman of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) from 2017 to 2022?
explain: Ajay Tyagi headed SEBI from March 2017 to early 2022. Urjit Patel was an RBI Governor and Ram Sewak Sharma has headed TRAI.

q: The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) was set up with the guidance and support of which institution?
explain: NPCI, the umbrella organisation for retail payments, was set up with the guidance and support of the Reserve Bank of India and the IBA.

q: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) is a quasi-judicial body that adjudicates issues relating to which of the following?
explain: NCLT deals with corporate disputes under company law, i.e. issues of Indian companies such as insolvency, mergers and oppression of minority.

q: Where was the Indian Banks' Association formed?
explain: IBA was formed in Mumbai on 26 September 1946.

q: How many banks were represented by the IBA when it was formed in 1946?
explain: IBA began with 22 member banks in 1946 and now represents several hundred banking companies (246 per the 2024-25 syllabus book).

q: How many Deputy Chairmen are there in the managing committee of the IBA?
explain: The managing committee has 1 Chairman, 3 Deputy Chairmen, 1 Honorary Secretary and 26 members.

q: How many ordinary members, apart from the Chairman, Deputy Chairmen and Honorary Secretary, sit on the IBA managing committee?
explain: The committee is 1 + 3 + 1 + 26: the 26 members are in addition to the Chairman, three Deputy Chairmen and one Honorary Secretary.

q: Where is the Banks Board Bureau housed?
options: Finance Ministry office in New Delhi
The central office of the RBI in Mumbai
NITI Aayog office in New Delhi
explain: The BBB is housed in the RBI's central office in Mumbai, though it is a separate autonomous, recommendatory body.

q: The Banks Board Bureau is considered the first step towards which institution recommended by the P J Nayak Committee?
explain: The P J Nayak Committee proposed a Bank Investment Company to hold government stakes in PSBs; the BBB is seen as the first step towards it.

q: The Banks Board Bureau was announced in August 2015 as part of which programme?
explain: The BBB is one of the seven points of the Indradhanush mission to revamp public sector banks.

q: How many ex-officio members (from the Government) are in the Banks Board Bureau besides the Chairman?
explain: There are 3 ex-officio members and 3 expert members; six in all besides the Chairman.

q: Of the three expert members of the Banks Board Bureau, how many are from the private sector?
explain: Two of the three expert members come from the private sector.

q: Which description fits the Banks Board Bureau best?
options: A statutory regulator that cancels bank licences
A section of the Finance Ministry secretariat
An autonomous recommendatory body for public sector banks
A private council of bank CEOs
explain: The Bureau is autonomous and recommendatory: it advises the Government, which makes the final appointments.

q: What happened on 28 February 2016 in the story of the Banks Board Bureau?
options: The Government announced the constitution and composition of the Bureau
The P J Nayak Committee submitted its report
The Bureau recommended its first bank chief
explain: The constitution and composition were announced on 28 February 2016; actual functioning began on 1 April 2016.

q: Which body replaced the Banks Board Bureau in 2022 for selecting heads of public sector financial institutions?
options: Banking Codes and Standards Board of India
Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India
explain: The Financial Services Institutions Bureau (FSIB) took over the BBB's selection role in 2022.

q: Which statement about the Indian Banks' Association is correct?
options: It is a statutory regulator formed under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
It represents only public sector banks
It was set up by the RBI in 2016 to replace the Appointments Board
It was formed in 1946 as a representative body of bank management
explain: IBA is an association of banks and financial institutions formed on 26 September 1946. It is not a regulator and is not limited to public sector banks.

q: Who was the first Chairman of the Banks Board Bureau?
explain: Vinod Rai, a former CAG, was the first Chairman of the BBB. P J Nayak chaired the committee that proposed it.

q: Which of these is a task of the Banks Board Bureau?
options: Advising PSBs on strategies to raise funds and handle stressed assets
explain: The Bureau advises PSBs on fund-raising strategies and stressed assets. Repo rate, banknotes and deposit insurance belong to the RBI and DICGC.
